claims.text: Optimized plasma nitriding of Ti-6Al-4V creates a thin, uniform, well-adhered TiN surface layer with a graded nitride zone.
The plasma-nitrided Ti-6Al-4V surface will have 50–100% greater hardness than untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Plasma nitriding will significantly enhance the wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V under sliding and cyclic loads.
The initial Ti-6Al-4V alloy is in an annealed and pre-polished state.
A nitrogen-hydrogen plasma treatment at approximately 450 °C for 6–8 hours is an optimized processing range for Ti-6Al-4V.
Refining plasma pressure, gas composition, and duration will ensure uniform TiN formation and robust adhesion.
The proposed improvement will hold at ambient and moderately elevated temperatures.
Ball-on-disk testing can evaluate the claimed performance under both sliding and cyclic loading conditions.
Nitrogen diffuses into the near-surface region of Ti-6Al-4V and reacts with titanium to form TiN.
TiN is a hard ceramic phase.
The nitrided layer increases hardness through combined solid-solution and precipitation strengthening.
A hard surface layer can resist plowing and reduce wear during frictional contact.
A protective surface layer can act as a barrier that improves wear resistance.
Untreated Ti-6Al-4V has lower surface hardness and higher wear rates than the proposed plasma-nitrided state under comparable conditions.
The treatment-induced changes are confined to the surface region and do not adversely affect bulk mechanical properties.
Performance gains depend on maintaining plasma-processing parameters within an optimized range.
Coating uniformity and adhesion depend on precise control of plasma parameters.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes treatment under 'inert conditions' while also specifying a reactive nitrogen-hydrogen plasma and a mechanism requiring nitrogen to react with titanium. The intended atmosphere is therefore internally ambiguous.
